Using the full OpenAlex snapshot, we identify thousands of concepts by\ntitle matching, track their adoption episodes across scientific fields, and\nscreen early network indicators against a popularity baseline on held out field\ngroups never used in selection. Seven indicators survive multiple testing\ncorrection, and a learned model combining them exceeds the baseline by\n$+0.059$ in Spearman correlation for predicting rarefied cross field breadth.\nThe retained frontier hypothesis, that concepts next enter fields related to the\nones currently retaining them, is confirmed in a preregistered held out test:\nconditional logit coefficient $d_0 = 0.322$ [$0.291$, $0.355$], positive in all\nfour domain groups. This extends the principle of\nrelatedness from economic geography to science, with the novel element that\nretention, not merely initial adoption, predicts where a concept goes next.\nA decomposition shows that 73\\% of the breadth gap between integrating and\nlocalised concepts is early contact diversity, while frontier advance\ncontributes near zero. The signal is topical nonredundancy of the early\nneighbourhood, not temporal partner turnover.\n\\end{abstract}\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Introduction}\n\\label{sec:introduction}\n\nSome scientific concepts stay within their home discipline for decades, while\nothers cross field boundaries within a few years. Optogenetics, originating in\nneuroscience, entered genetics, psychiatry and bioengineering; deep learning,\nrooted in computer science, now appears in medicine, materials science and\nlinguistics. Understanding what distinguishes broadly diffusing concepts from\nlocally absorbed ones matters for science policy, research evaluation and the\ndesign of interdisciplinary programmes \\citep{Cheng2023, Hofstra2019}. If early\nstructural signals predict later cross field integration, funders and\ninstitutions could identify concepts with high diffusion potential before that\ndiffusion is observable in publication counts alone.\n\nThe problem is hard because simple popularity metrics, including publication\nvolume, growth rate and off home publication share, already explain much of the\nvariance in later breadth \\citep{Rotolo2015}. Any network indicator must add\ninformation beyond these baselines. Prior work has proposed several candidate\nsignals: community diversity of early adopters \\citep{Weng2013}, collaboration\ndensity before emergence \\citep{Salatino2017}, and structural variation in\ncitation networks \\citep{Salatino2018}. These studies typically operate on\ncurated concept sets without held out validation, mix units of analysis defined\nat the level of individual concepts with those at the field level, or do not\ncontrol for volume based predictors.\nNo prior study has screened a broad set of temporal knowledge network indicators\nagainst a shared baseline on held out field groups for the specific outcome of\nsize adjusted interdisciplinary breadth.\n\nA second open question concerns the routes by which concepts move between\nfields. The principle of relatedness, established for regional economic\ndiversification, predicts that actors diversify into activities related to their\nexisting portfolio. For scientific fields adopting new concepts, this principle\nhas been tested for entry but not for the role of currently retaining fields,\nthose that have adopted a concept and kept publishing on it. Whether concepts\nspread next to fields related to the ones currently retaining them, beyond\nrelatedness to the home field alone, is untested.\n\nThis paper addresses both questions with a large scale empirical study. We\nidentify 12,499 concepts from the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (476 million works),\ncompute 53 early network indicators across seven families, and test them on\nheld out field groups and a confirmatory onset cohort. We build a\nconditional logit model, a discrete choice model that estimates the probability\nof entry into each candidate field within a stratified choice set, to test\nwhether retained field\nrelatedness predicts the next field a concept enters. We decompose the breadth\ngap between integrating and localised concepts into early contact, frontier\nadvance and retention channels.\n\nOur contributions are:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item We screen 53 early co-occurrence network indicators against a\n    five feature popularity baseline and confirm seven on held out field groups\n    for predicting rarefied cross field breadth, with an ElasticNet combining\n    them exceeding the baseline by $+0.059$ [$+0.046$, $+0.073$] in Spearman\n    correlation.\n  \\item We confirm, in a preregistered test on 3,162 held out concepts, that\n    concepts spread next to fields related to the ones currently retaining them\n    (conditional logit $d_0 = 0.322$ [$0.291$, $0.355$]), extending the principle\n    of relatedness to concept diffusion in science.\n  \\item We decompose the breadth gap between widely and narrowly spreading\n    concepts: 73\\% is early contact diversity, near 0\\% is frontier advance,\n    and 25\\% is differential retention.\n  \\item We show that early neighbourhood consolidation, measured by ideational\n    consistency, predicts volume growth but narrower cross field reach, a\n    reversal that holds in all five domain groups.\n  \\item We replicate the openness signal on a fresh 2015--2017 cohort (partial\n    Spearman $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$]) and on vocabulary free newborn\n    phrases.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe remainder of the paper is organised as follows. Section~\\ref{sec:related}\nsurveys related work. Section~\\ref{sec:methods} describes the data,\nindicators and models. Section~\\ref{sec:results} presents results.\nSection~\\ref{sec:discussion} discusses the findings, and\nSection~\\ref{sec:limitations} states limitations.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Related Work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{Concept diffusion in science.}\n\\citet{Cheng2023} tracked roughly 2,000 new ideas across Web of Science fields\nand found that early social reach, the number of disconnected researcher groups\nadopting an idea, was the strongest predictor of whether an idea became core.\nTheir ideational consistency measure, the cosine similarity of vectors recording which topics a concept's neighbours\nuse across consecutive years, predicted next year volume.\n\\citet{Rotolo2015} defined emerging technologies through five attributes\nincluding novelty and fast growth but did not test cross field spread.\n\\citet{Salatino2017} showed that collaboration density rises before topic\nemergence. These studies provide the starting point for our work but do not\nscreen a broad indicator set against a shared baseline with held out validation\nfor size adjusted cross field breadth.\n\n\\paragraph{Topic co-occurrence and citation networks.}\n\\citet{Callon1991} introduced co-word analysis as a tool for mapping the\nstructure of research fields. \\citet{Chavalarias2013} found that dense term\nclusters survive longer, and that density rises during emergence and falls\nbefore decline. \\citet{Salatino2018} proposed the AUGUR system for detecting\ntopic emergence from co-occurrence backbone dynamics. Our work differs in that\nwe test co-occurrence indicators as predictors of a specific outcome, cross field\nbreadth, rather than using them descriptively.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty, recombination and impact.}\n\\citet{Uzzi2013} found that high impact papers combine conventional and atypical\njournal pairings. \\citet{Hofstra2019} documented the diversity--innovation\nparadox: researchers from underrepresented groups produce more novel work but\nreceive fewer citations. \\citet{Tria2013} modelled the dynamics of correlated\nnovelties, showing that novelty begets novelty through the adjacent possible.\n\\citet{Burt2004} showed that structural holes, brokerage positions spanning\ndisconnected groups, generate good ideas. These studies operate at the paper or\nindividual level; ours operates at the concept level and asks about cross field\nbreadth rather than citation impact.\n\n\\paragraph{The principle of relatedness.}\n\\citet{Hidalgo2007} showed that a country's position in the product space\npredicts which products it diversifies into. \\citet{Neffke2011} extended this to\nregional industry diversification. Our contribution is to test whether\nrelatedness to the set of fields currently retaining a concept predicts entry,\nbeyond relatedness to the home field and conventional density measures.\n\n\\paragraph{Community structure and virality.}\n\\citet{Weng2013} showed that early community diversity predicts virality of\nonline content (AUC $= 0.83$). \\citet{Ugander2012} found that structural\ndiversity drives social contagion on Facebook. \\citet{Centola2010} demonstrated\nexperimentally that complex contagions require reinforcement from multiple\ncommunities. \\citet{Palla2007} tracked the evolution of overlapping communities\nin large networks. Our indicator screen tests the scholarly analogue of these\nmechanisms: whether a concept's early co-occurrence partners spanning multiple\ncommunities predicts later cross field breadth.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Data and Methods}\n\\label{sec:methods}\n\n\\subsection{Concept identification and panel construction}\n\nWe use the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (476,196,327 works; 129.4 million base works\n1995--2022). Concepts are identified by Aho--Corasick title matching of 56,643\nlegacy OpenAlex concepts (levels 2--5) plus Wikidata aliases, with stemmed\nverification. A per concept precision gate drops concepts with precision below\n0.80 (benchmark precision 0.947, recall 0.659, assessed on a benchmark of 390 pairs\nwith 60 hand checked pairs at 90\\% agreement).\n\nA concept's onset year $t_0$ is the first year it reaches 20 grounded\npublications. Home fields are the fields holding at least 40\\% of the first 30\ngrounded papers. The frame comprises 12,499 concepts and 27,393 adoption episodes (one per\nconcept--field pair).\n\nThe panel is split by home field family into a development set (DEV: Computer\nScience, Engineering, Biochemistry/Genetics/Medicine; 4,771 concepts), four\nheld out field groups (Physical Sciences 742, Life and Environment 1,113, Social\nSciences 1,352, Mathematics and Decision Sciences 165), and a 2010--2014 onset\ncohort (4,356 concepts, all fields). The specification was hash sealed on DEV\nbefore held out scoring.\n\n\\subsection{Field backbone}\n\nThe interfield backbone is a weighted graph over 26 fields, with edge weights\ngiven by positive pointwise mutual information (PMI) of topics appearing jointly\nin the same work within a preonset window (1998--2002). This backbone is used throughout for relatedness\ndensity, gateway centrality and community detection. Its time varying versions\n(computed in five year slices) correlate at Spearman 0.92 with the frozen version.\n\n\\subsection{Outcome: rarefied cross field breadth}\n\nThe primary outcome is rarefied cross field breadth $O_{2r}$ ($m = 50$): the\nexpected number of distinct venue fields among a fixed size random draw of 50\npapers from a concept's publications in years $t_0 + 6$ to $t_0 + 8$, computed\nby exact hypergeometric rarefaction. Rarefaction separates size adjusted breadth\nfrom sheer volume. Secondary outcomes include sustained uptake, transience, and\nfield- and year normalised citation growth.\n\n\\subsection{Baseline}\n\nThe five feature popularity baseline is: log publication volume at\n$t_0 + 2$, publication growth rate, log off home volume, off home share, and\nnumber of home fields. This baseline alone reaches Spearman correlations of 0.65--0.86 with\n$O_{2r}$ across domain groups, setting a high bar for incremental network\nindicators.\n\n\\subsection{Indicator families}\n\nWe compute 53 indicators across seven families in the $t_0$ to $t_0 + 2$\nwindow:\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\textbf{Popularity (E):} publication growth, author growth, author count.\n  \\item \\textbf{Disciplinary composition (F):} Shannon entropy of field\n    distribution, home field relatedness, Rao--Stirling diversity.\n  \\item \\textbf{Landing position (G):} gateway centrality of home and early\n    off home fields.\n  \\item \\textbf{Retained frontier (FR):} relatedness density to fields with\n    revealed comparative advantage (RCA) $> 1$, volume weighted density, contact\n    reach (count of off home fields entered), retention ratio (share of contacted\n    fields that retain the concept).\n  \\item \\textbf{Co-occurrence ego network (A):} 27 indicators from the\n    concept's ego network on the co-occurrence backbone, including neighbourhood\n    novelty (share of new partners), edge persistence (share of retained\n    partners), number of Leiden communities among neighbours, ego density,\n    participation coefficient, brokerage.\n  \\item \\textbf{Author overlap ties (S):} shared authorship between concepts.\n  \\item \\textbf{External recognition:} whether the concept appears in domain\n    taxonomies or curated lists.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\subsection{Indicator selection and validation}\n\nIndicators are screened on DEV by partial Spearman correlation with $O_{2r}$\ngiven the popularity baseline, using leaving one home group out cross validation\nwith 2,000 bootstrap resamples of concepts. The top 10 frozen indicators per outcome\nare evaluated on held out groups with DerSimonian--Laird random effects pooling\nacross four domain groups and Holm--Bonferroni correction for multiplicity (a\nstepdown procedure controlling the familywise error rate).\n\n\\subsection{Retained frontier model}\n\nFor the field entry analysis, we construct risk sets indexed by concept, target\nfield and year: at each year after onset, every off home field that the concept\nhas not yet entered is at risk. Entry is defined as the concept reaching 5 grounded\npublications in the field. The conditional logit (Breslow partial likelihood) is\nstratified by each combination of concept and year, with standardised covariates\nadded in four nested\nrungs: the baseline includes relatedness to home, log field size, entered field\ndensity based on revealed comparative advantage and own field gateway centrality;\nthe second rung adds density of fields with revealed comparative advantage above\nunity; the third adds volume weighted density; and the full model adds\nretained field relatedness $d_0$, defined as the mean backbone relatedness\nbetween the target field and the set of off home fields currently retaining the\nconcept. The specification is frozen on DEV and scored once on the held out\nframe.\n\n\\subsection{Breadth decomposition}\n\nWe decompose the gap in retained off home breadth at $t_0 + 8$ between the top\nand bottom $O_{2r}$ terciles into three multiplicative factors: early contact\n$E_2$ (fields entered by $t_0 + 2$), frontier advance $M$ (ratio of fields\nentered by $t_0 + 8$ to those entered by $t_0 + 2$), and retention ratio\n$\\rho$ (share of entered fields retained at $t_0 + 8$). The decomposition is\nvolume stratified.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\n\\subsection{Which indicators predict cross field breadth?}\n\nSeven of the 53 screened indicators survive held out validation with\nHolm--Bonferroni correction for predicting rarefied cross field breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$),\nall positive in six of six domain groups and cohort bodies\n(Table~\\ref{tab:confirmed}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Confirmed indicators for rarefied cross field breadth ($O_{2r}$,\n$m=50$). Pooled partial Spearman correlations from DerSimonian--Laird\nrandom effects pooling across four held out domain groups. All seven\nsurvive Holm--Bonferroni correction.}\n\\label{tab:confirmed}\n\\begin{tabularx}{\\linewidth}{>{\\raggedright\\arraybackslash}p{4.2cm} c c c c}\n\\toprule\nIndicator & Family & Pooled $\\rho$ & 95\\% CI & $I^2$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nCumulative density of entered fields & FR & $+0.375$ & $[+0.279, +0.462]$ & 0.74 \\\\\nVolume weighted density & FR & $+0.307$ & $[+0.256, +0.356]$ & 0.10 \\\\\nContact reach (off home fields entered) & FR & $+0.211$ & $[+0.161, +0.261]$ & 0.00 \\\\\nCommunities among co-occurrence neighbours & A & $+0.167$ & $[+0.063, +0.267]$ & 0.78 \\\\\nNeighbourhood novelty & A & $+0.151$ & $[+0.044, +0.255]$ & 0.75 \\\\\nRetention ratio of contacted fields & FR & $-0.114$ & $[-0.160, -0.067]$ & 0.00 \\\\\nEgo network density & A & $-0.102$ & $[-0.151, -0.053]$ & 0.00 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabularx}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe first two indicators, cumulative density and volume weighted density, use\nthe cumulative field history up to $t_0 + 2$ and partly reflect a preonset\nfootprint. After removing the preonset component, the postonset\nvolume weighted density attenuates to about half its raw value ($+0.176$ vs\n$+0.307$) and is nearly rank identical to the popularity baseline (Spearman\nbetween the two $> 0.97$). The remaining indicators, contact reach, community\ncount, novelty, retention ratio and ego density, measure genuinely early\nstructural properties.\n\nA learned ElasticNet combining the confirmed indicators exceeds the popularity\nbaseline by $+0.059$ [$+0.046$, $+0.073$] in Spearman correlation on the pooled\nheld out set. Held out increments by domain group are: Physical Sciences\n$+0.050$, Life and\nEnvironment $+0.059$, Social Sciences $+0.062$, Mathematics and Decision\nSciences $+0.037$.\n\nFor sustained uptake, only the number of early authors is confirmed. For\ncitation growth, home field relatedness (negative) and author growth are\nconfirmed but the learned model reaches only Spearman 0.188 against the popularity baseline's 0.015.\nExternal recognition shows no association with any network indicator beyond\nonset year.\n\n\\subsection{Openness composite and confirmation}\n\nThe six ego network components of the confirmed indicators compose into an\nopenness index (OPEN), defined as the mean of six $z$-scored components with\nconstants frozen on the full frame of all 12,499 concepts.\n\nOn a fresh 2015--2017 onset cohort of 1,443 concepts never used in any selection\nstep, OPEN measured within the home field (OPEN\\textsubscript{home}) shows a\npartial Spearman correlation with $O_{2r}$ of $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$] at\nthe second control rung (controlling for the popularity baseline, onset year and contact reach), and\n$+0.080$ [$+0.001$, $+0.162$] at the third rung (adding concept type and\npreonset footprint). The confidence interval includes zero at higher rungs, and\nthe DerSimonian--Laird pool across groups is $+0.083$ [$-0.007$, $+0.173$]. The\nsignal carries no forecasting gain over the popularity baseline ($+0.002$ Spearman). The\npreregistered verdict is confirmed but marginal.\n\nAn evidence synthesis across six nonselection bodies (four held out domain\ngroups plus the 2010--2014 and 2015--2017 cohorts) gives a DerSimonian--Laird\npooled OPEN\\textsubscript{home} partial Spearman of $+0.069$ [$+0.038$,\n$+0.100$] with $I^2 = 0$, all six bodies positive. The selection body (DEV)\nestimate of $+0.109$ shows shrinkage of $1.58\\times$ relative to the\nnonselection pool.\n\nNeighbourhood novelty carries the openness signal. The pooled partial Spearman\nof neighbourhood novelty and churn across five nonselection bodies is $+0.105$\n[$+0.069$, $+0.140$] with $I^2 = 0$, while edge persistence is null on the\nfresh cohort. Figure~\\ref{fig:evidence_synthesis} summarises the evidence\nacross all evaluation bodies.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig2_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Partial Spearman correlation between home field openness (OPEN\\_home) and rarefied cross field breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m=50$), controlling for the popularity baseline (second control rung), per evaluation body. Blue squares are the six nonselection bodies: four held out domain groups and the 2010--14 and 2015--17 onset cohorts. Square area is proportional to inverse variance (Fisher-$z$) weight, and horizontal lines are 95\\% bootstrap CIs (2,000 bootstrap resamples of concepts); $n$ is the number of concepts analysed. The blue diamond spans the DerSimonian--Laird random effects pool over these six bodies, $+0.069$ [$+0.038$, $+0.100$] with $I^2=0$, and the dotted blue line marks the pooled estimate. The grey row is the DEV selection body ($+0.109$ [$+0.073$, $+0.144$], $n=3{,}003$), on which the index was chosen. It is not part of the pool and is $1.58\\times$ the pooled estimate, consistent with winner's curse shrinkage. The dashed grey line marks zero. All six nonselection estimates are positive, but only the two cohort intervals exclude zero. Because five of the six bodies had been unsealed earlier, the pool is descriptive rather than confirmatory.}\n  \\label{fig:evidence_synthesis}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsection{Confound analysis: topical dispersion, not temporal churn}\n\nThe openness signal could be an artefact of small yearly samples. We test this\nwith four null models:\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\textbf{Fixed-$n$ rarefaction null} (drawing $n = 10$ partners per\n    year): neighbourhood novelty and churn retains 68\\% of the raw effect\n    (pooled $+0.078$ vs $+0.116$).\n  \\item \\textbf{Temporal permutation null} (randomly reordering the year labels\n    within each concept's own time series, 200 permutations): the temporal excess is $+0.008$\n    with split half reliability below 0.05, indicating that the temporal ordering\n    of partner arrivals contributes almost nothing.\n  \\item \\textbf{Configuration model null} (rewiring the ego network while\n    preserving each node's degree, following the Molloy--Reed configuration\n    model): ego density normalised against the null ($z$-scored) still predicts\n    breadth (partial Spearman $-0.091$).\n  \\item \\textbf{Split half reliability}: neighbourhood novelty and churn\n    raw $= 0.48$, OPEN\\textsubscript{home} $= 0.49$, rising to 0.58 after\n    configuration model cleaning.\n\\end{itemize}\n\nRaw edge persistence is 66\\% explained by its own temporal permutation null mean\n(computed by reordering year labels within each concept's time series), and that null mean predicts the\noutcome at least as strongly as raw\npersistence itself. The signal is a static topical dispersion property of the\nhome topic mix, not temporal partner turnover.\n\n\\subsection{Reconciling consistency and breadth}\n\n\\citet{Cheng2023} reported that ideational consistency (cosine of a concept's\ntopic usage vector across consecutive years) predicts next year volume with\na 53\\% increase per standard deviation. We reproduce this almost exactly: our\ntwin negative binomial model gives $+53.5\\%$ per SD. Adding log current volume\nreduces this to $+1.3\\%$ [$+0.5\\%$, $+2.1\\%$]: the raw association is\nsize dominated.\n\nNet of size, consistency's partial Spearman with rarefied cross field breadth is\n$-0.069$ [$-0.093$, $-0.047$], negative in all five domain groups. On the\n2015--2017 cohort, the reversal replicates at $-0.111$ [$-0.197$, $-0.030$].\nPanel analysis tracking each concept over time shows that years of high\nconsistency are followed by slightly more off home entries ($b = +0.025$\n[$+0.004$, $+0.048$]), so the reach penalty is a trait observed across concepts, not a mechanism operating within a single\nconcept over time.\n\nConsistency and breadth are not opposed within a single concept's trajectory, but\nconcepts whose neighbourhood is consistently structured tend to grow in volume\nrather than spreading across fields. This complements \\citet{Cheng2023} by\nseparating the volume and breadth outcomes.\n\n\\subsection{How do concepts diffuse across fields?}\n\n\\subsubsection{Retained frontier entry}\n\nThe conditional logit model tests whether a concept's next field of entry is\npredicted by the target field's relatedness to the off home fields that\ncurrently retain the concept, beyond relatedness to the home field, field size,\nentered field density and own gateway centrality.\n\nOn the development frame (274 concepts, 961 informative strata), the model\nreproduces a prior result: likelihood ratio 68.6, $d_0 = 0.281$.\n\nOn the independent held out frame (3,162 concepts, 6,978 entry events,\nhash frozen specification), the retained frontier coefficient is $d_0 = 0.322$\n[$0.291$, $0.355$] with standard errors clustered by concept (likelihood ratio\n325.8 for the retained frontier term over the volume density rung,\n$p < 10^{-72}$). The result is positive in all four\nheld out domain groups: Physical Sciences 0.148, Life and Environment 0.401,\nSocial Sciences 0.297, Mathematics and Decision Sciences 0.065\n(underpowered). The DerSimonian--Laird pool over four groups gives 0.243\n[$0.118$, $0.368$] with $I^2 = 0.92$, reflecting genuine heterogeneity across\ndomains. Three permutation tests confirm robustness: shuffling which fields\nretain the concept ($p = 0.001$), rewiring the field backbone ($p = 0.004$),\nand permuting concept labels across nodes ($p = 0.003$).\n\nThe predeclared volume matched contrast, comparing entry rates of retained\nversus fields that were entered but not retained in the same volume cell, is null:\n$-0.028$ [$-0.105$, $+0.046$]. The frozen verdict is therefore partial:\npersistence is confounded with volume. Under a minimum conditional probability\nproximity \\citep{Hidalgo2007}, the retained frontier coefficient reverses to\n$-0.021$ ($p = 0.012$), indicating backbone dependence.\nTable~\\ref{tab:retained_frontier} reports all estimates by domain group.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Retained frontier coefficient $d_0$ from the conditional logit model\nof next field entry across domain groups and the 2010--2014 cohort, with 95\\%\nconfidence intervals clustered by concept.}\n\\label{tab:retained_frontier}\n\\begin{tabular}{l c c c}\n\\toprule\nModel & $d_0$ coefficient & 95\\% CI (concept) & Likelihood ratio \\\\\n\\midrule\nDevelopment set & 0.228 & $[0.164, 0.291]$ & 34.5 \\\\\nHeld out pooled & 0.322 & $[0.291, 0.355]$ & 325.8 \\\\\nPhysical Sciences & 0.148 & $[0.078, 0.219]$ & -- \\\\\nLife \\& Environment & 0.401 & $[0.342, 0.460]$ & -- \\\\\nSocial Sciences & 0.297 & $[0.246, 0.348]$ & -- \\\\\nMath \\& Decision Sci. & 0.065 & $[-0.109, 0.239]$ & -- \\\\\n2010--2014 cohort & 0.321 & $[0.292, 0.347]$ & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig3_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained frontier coefficient $d_0$ from the conditional logit model of next field entry, estimated on held out data. $d_0$ measures how much a target field's relatedness to the fields currently retaining a concept predicts entry into it. It is net of relatedness to the home field, field size, entered field density and gateway centrality, and is expressed in log odds per standard deviation. Blue circles are the estimates for the four held out domain groups (top) and for the 2010--14 held out cohort. Horizontal bars are 95\\% Wald confidence intervals from standard errors clustered by concept, and $n$ is the number of entry events. The dark diamond spans the DerSimonian--Laird random effects pooled estimate over the four groups, 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], with $I^2 = 0.92$. The dashed vertical line marks $d_0 = 0$, and the right hand column prints each estimate with its interval. The point estimate is positive in all four groups and in the cohort. The interval excludes zero for Physical Sciences, Life \\& Env., Social Sciences and the cohort. Math \\& Decision ($n = 296$) is the weak, imprecise group, 0.065 [$-0.109$, 0.239], and together with Life \\& Env.\\ (0.401) it drives the high heterogeneity. These are associations. In the same experiment, a volume matched contrast between retaining and nonretaining fields is null ($-0.028$ [$-0.105$, 0.046]; not plotted), so the preregistered frontier test is only partially supported: persistence is confounded with volume.}\n  \\label{fig:retained_frontier}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig4_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Nested conditional logit models of field entry on the held out frame (3,162 concepts, 6,978 entry events, 6,076 informative strata, one per combination of concept and year). The baseline rung includes home relatedness, log field size, entered field density and own field gateway centrality; successive rungs add density of fields with revealed comparative advantage above unity, then volume weighted density, then retained frontier relatedness. (a)~AUC computed within each stratum for each rung. Blue circles, solid line: primary specification using backbone relatedness. Amber squares, dashed line: sensitivity rebuild using minimum conditional probability proximity. (b)~Likelihood ratio $\\chi^2$ (df $=1$, log scale) for the term each rung adds over the previous rung. Solid blue bars: primary. Hatched amber bars: sensitivity. The dotted line marks $p=0.05$ ($\\chi^2=3.84$). In the primary specification, the retained frontier term gives the largest step (LR $=325.8$, $p<10^{-72}$), but AUC rises only from 0.847 to 0.852. The volume density step is not significant (LR $=1.9$). Under minimum conditional probability proximity, baseline discrimination is higher and the retained frontier term adds no AUC (0.867 to 0.866; LR $=6.3$). The increment therefore depends on the proximity definition. No confidence intervals on AUC are available.}\n  \\label{fig:model_ladder}\n\\end{figure}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:retained_frontier} shows the estimates by domain group, and\nFigure~\\ref{fig:model_ladder} displays the nested model ladder. The\nAUC within each stratum increases from 0.847 before adding the\nretained frontier term to 0.852 after. The increment is small\nbecause field size alone achieves AUC 0.76, density only 0.59, and the ceiling\nis constrained by having only 26 fields.\n\n\\subsubsection{Gateway centrality does not predict retention}\n\nA separate preregistered test asks whether the adopting field's eigenvector\ncentrality on the backbone predicts retention. On 27,393 held out episodes, the\ngateway centrality increment is effectively zero: $\\Delta$-AUC $-0.00001$\n[$-0.0006$, $+0.0003$]. The minimum detectable effect is 0.004. Gateway alone\nhas AUC 0.605 on DEV versus 0.506 on held out: the DEV signal is\ndomain specific. Verdict: disconfirmed.\n\n\\subsubsection{Breadth decomposition}\n\nWe decompose the gap in retained off home breadth between the top and bottom\n$O_{2r}$ terciles into log $E_2$ (early contact), log $M$ (frontier advance)\nand log $\\rho$ (retention). Volume stratified, on the held out pool excluding\nMedicine (to avoid a domain that dominates the localised class):\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item Early contact share: 73.3\\%\n  \\item Frontier advance share: 1.3\\%\n  \\item Retention share: 25.4\\%\n  \\item Difference (exploration minus retention): 0.492 [$0.403$, $0.575$]\n\\end{itemize}\n\nThe DerSimonian--Laird pool of the exploration minus retention difference across three\nheld out groups is 0.504 [$0.329$, $0.679$] with $I^2 = 0.76$.\n\nBreadth differences between concepts are set by how many fields a concept\ncontacts early, not by how many more it enters later. Frontier advance, the\nratio of fields at $t_0 + 8$ to those at $t_0 + 2$, contributes near zero\nbecause both broad and narrow concepts gain new fields at similar rates relative\nto their base (Figure~\\ref{fig:decomposition}).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig5_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Decomposition of the gap in retained off home breadth (log scale) between the top and bottom $O_{2r}$ tercile into three multiplicative channels: early contact ($E_2$, green), frontier advance ($M$, light grey) and retention ($\\rho$, blue). The left bar stacks the three shares into the total gap (share $=1$; total log gap $D_{\\text{total}}=1.035$, 95\\% CI $[0.957, 1.108]$). The other three bars show each channel's share of the gap with 95\\% percentile confidence intervals from 2{,}000 bootstrap resamples of concepts, with terciles and volume quintiles recomputed in each resample. The sample is the held out pool (PHYS, LIFEENV, SOC, MATHDEC), volume stratified, excluding Medicine homes ($n=1{,}825$ concepts). Early contact accounts for 73\\% of the gap (0.733, $[0.688, 0.789]$), retention for 25\\% (0.254, $[0.213, 0.298]$), and frontier advance for close to zero (0.013, $[-0.027, 0.047]$). The shares are an accounting identity for the breadth outcome, not causal effects.}\n  \\label{fig:decomposition}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{Diffusion trajectories: a continuum, not types}\n\nWe tested whether concepts cluster into discrete trajectory types (localised\nemergence, rapid interdisciplinary diffusion, gradual integration) using DTW\n$k$-medoids and hidden Markov model (HMM) clustering on state sequences of\nfield presence. No trajectory typology passes a naming rule: the adjusted Rand\nindex between DTW $k = 4$ and HMM $S = 5$ is 0.222, and held out reclustering\ngives ARI $= 0.44$. Instead, PCA reveals a continuum: the first principal\ncomponent (38.8\\% of variance) is a breadth axis, and the second principal\ncomponent (10.7\\%) is a keep versus lose axis. Early openness (OPEN) correlates\nwith the first principal component beyond the popularity baseline (held out\nDerSimonian--Laird partial correlation 0.120, $I^2 = 0$) but not with the\nsecond.\n\n\\subsection{Replication on vocabulary free concepts}\n\nTo test whether the openness signal depends on the legacy concept lexicon, we\nconstructed a separate frame of 636 newborn title noun phrases (onsets\n2003--2015) absent from the 56,643 legacy concepts. On this frame,\nOPEN\\textsubscript{home} shows a partial Spearman with rarefied breadth\n($O_{2r}$, $m = 30$) of $+0.117$ [$+0.020$, $+0.218$] at the third control\nrung, and neighbourhood novelty and churn of $+0.108$ [$+0.007$, $+0.211$].\nThree of four estimable domain groups are positive. The verdict is partial: the\nconfidence interval on OPEN\\textsubscript{home} includes zero at the fifth\ncontrol rung, and the $p$-value after Holm--Bonferroni correction is 0.052.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\nOur results address both research questions posed in the Introduction.\n\nFor the first research question, seven temporal network indicators predict\ncross field breadth beyond a strong popularity baseline, and these indicators\ngeneralise across four held out scientific domain groups. The strongest are contact reach (the count of off home\nfields already entered) and neighbourhood novelty (the share of new\nco-occurrence partners). A learned model improves Spearman correlation by\n$+0.059$ over the baseline. The practical forecasting gain is modest: the popularity baseline already\nexplains most of the variance, and OPEN adds only $+0.002$ Spearman on the\nfresh cohort. The signal identifies which concepts are structurally positioned\nfor broader diffusion, rather than providing strong individual level forecasts.\n\nThe confound analysis reveals that the signal is topical nonredundancy, a\nstatic structural property of the home topic mix, rather than temporal partner\nturnover. A concept whose early partners span multiple communities and introduce\nnovel topical connections tends to spread more broadly, but this tendency is set\nby the concept's position in the knowledge network rather than by dynamic churn.\n\nFor the second research question, the retained frontier model confirms that concepts spread next to\nfields related to the ones currently retaining them. This extends the principle\nof relatedness from economic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007, Neffke2011}, where\nregions diversify into products related to their existing portfolio, to\nscientific concept diffusion. The novel element is retention: it is not merely\nwhich fields have adopted a concept that predicts the next field, but which of\nthose fields continue to use it. The volume matched contrast is null, however,\nindicating that retention and volume are confounded and that the pure retention\nsignal cannot be isolated at this sample size.\n\nThe breadth decomposition shows that the gap between integrating and localised\nconcepts is set early by contact diversity (73\\%) rather than by continued\nfrontier advance (1\\%). This echoes \\citet{Weng2013}, who found that early\ncommunity diversity predicts virality, and extends it from social media to\nscientific knowledge networks.\n\nThe reconciliation with \\citet{Cheng2023} reveals an outcome dependent split:\nconsistency predicts volume growth (size dominated) but narrower cross field\nreach. The two findings are compatible because volume growth and cross field\nbreadth are partially independent outcomes.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Limitations}\n\\label{sec:limitations}\n\nSeveral limitations bound the scope of these results.\n\nFirst, concept identification relies on title matching against a legacy lexicon\nthat overrepresents the natural sciences and computer science. The\nvocabulary free replication partially addresses this, but its sample is smaller\nand the verdict is partial.\n\nSecond, the field backbone uses a fixed classification of 26 fields from OpenAlex.\nA finer grained classification would produce more adoption episodes but also\nmore noise in field assignment. Our results are conditioned on this specific\nresolution.\n\nThird, the retained frontier claim is partial by its own preregistered rule:\nthe volume matched contrast is null, meaning that we cannot distinguish the\neffect of retention from that of volume. A larger sample with more fine grained\nvolume controls would be needed to isolate pure retention.\n\nFourth, the openness signal's practical forecasting value is small ($+0.002$\nSpearman on the fresh cohort). The indicators characterise rather than predict:\nthey identify structural preconditions for broad diffusion but do not yield\nindividually actionable forecasts.\n\nFifth, outcomes are measured at $t_0 + 6$ to $t_0 + 8$, a horizon of 6--8\nyears after concept onset. Longer horizons might reveal different dynamics, and\nour results do not speak to very long term disciplinary integration.\n\nSixth, the analysis is observational. Early network structure is correlated with\nlater breadth, but we cannot establish that it causes broader diffusion. The\npanel analysis tracking each concept over time suggests that the association is a\ntrait observed across concepts rather than a mechanism operating within a single\nconcept's trajectory.\n\nSeventh, the held out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier\nexperiments in the same project, so the indicator screen held out results are\nrobustness checks within the same frame rather than fully independent\nconfirmations. The fresh 2015--2017 cohort is the only body never used in any\nprior step.\n\nEighth, Mathematics and Decision Sciences is underpowered in both the indicator\nscreen (165 concepts) and the retained frontier model ($d_0 = 0.065$, CI\nincludes zero), so our results may not generalise to this domain.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\\label{sec:conclusion}\n\nWe have shown that early structural signals in a concept's co-occurrence network\npredict later cross field breadth across multiple scientific domains, that\nconcepts spread next to fields related to the ones currently retaining them, and\nthat early contact diversity, not continued frontier advance, accounts for most\nof the breadth difference between integrating and localised concepts. The\nopenness signal is topical nonredundancy of the home neighbourhood, not\ntemporal partner turnover. These findings connect the literatures on concept\ndiffusion in science \\citep{Cheng2023}, the principle of relatedness from\neconomic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007}, and community structure in social\ncontagion \\citep{Weng2013, Ugander2012}, offering a network level account of\nwhy some scientific concepts become broadly integrated while others remain local.\n\n%% ===================================================================\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 673, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 673}}

{"stdout": "# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- states\ndef panel_states(G: np.ndarray, home_mask: np.ndarray, min_n: float = 2) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"G [C, NY, 27] grounded counts (slot 0 = unlabelled venue); home_mask [C, 26] bool.\n    Returns [C, NY, 26] arrays (bool / int16 / float32).\"\"\"\n    x = G[:, :, 1:].astype(np.float64)\n    cum = np.cumsum(x, 1)\n    entered = cum >= min_n\n    w3 = x.copy()\n    w3[:, 1:] += x[:, :-1]\n    w3[:, 2:] += x[:, :-2]\n    ent_lag2 = np.zeros_like(entered)\n    ent_lag2[:, 2:] = entered[:, :-2]\n    offhome = ~home_mask\n    retaining = ent_lag2 & (w3 >= min_n) & offhome[:, None, :]\n    lost = entered & (w3 == 0)\n    yr = np.arange(NY, dtype=np.int16)\n    first = np.where(entered.any(1), entered.argmax(1), NY).astype(np.int16)  # [C, 26]\n    age = (yr[None, :, None] - first[:, None, :]).astype(np.int16)          # valid where entered\n    lastpos = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(x > 0, yr[None, :, None], -1), axis=1).astype(np.int16)\n    tenure = (lastpos - first[:, None, :]).astype(np.int16)                  # tenure of a LOST presence\n    return {\"x\": x.astype(np.float32), \"cum\": cum.astype(np.float32), \"w3\": w3.astype(np.float32),\n            \"entered\": entered, \"ent_lag2\": ent_lag2, \"retaining\": retaining, \"lost\": lost,\n            \"offhome\": offhome, \"age\": age, \"tenure\": tenure, \"first\": first}\n\n\ndef rca_entered_panel(G: np.ndarray, GF: np.ndarray, min_n: float = 2) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Vectorised h2_exp6.rca_entered: cum >= 2 AND cumulative share > field's cumulative share of all works; absorbing.\"\"\"\n    x = np.cumsum(G[:, :, 1:].astype(np.float64), 1)\n    tot = x.sum(2, keepdims=True)\n    F = np.cumsum(GF.astype(np.float64), 0)\n    share_all = F / np.maximum(F.sum(1, keepdims=True), 1)\n    share_c = x / np.maximum(tot, 1)\n    ok = (x >= min_n) & (share_c > share_all[None])\n    return np.maximum.accumulate(ok.astype(np.int8), 1).astype(bool)\n\n\ndef _rca(nc: np.ndarray, NT: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"nc [..., 26] concept counts, NT [..., 26] base totals broadcastable. RCA = (nc/sum nc) / (NT/sum NT); 0 if nc empty.\"\"\"\n    s = nc.sum(-1, keepdims=True)\n    share_c = nc / np.where(s > 0, s, 1)\n    share_all = NT / np.maximum(NT.sum(-1, keepdims=True), 1)\n    return np.where(s > 0, share_c / np.where(share_all > 0, share_all, np.inf), 0.0)\n\n\ndef rolling(a: np.ndarray, w: int, axis: int) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"sum over the trailing window [y-w+1, y] (partial at the start).\"\"\"\n    c = np.cumsum(a, axis)\n    out = c.copy()\n    sl = [slice(None)] * a.ndim\n    sl2 = [slice(None)] * a.ndim\n    sl[axis] = slice(w, None)\n    sl2[axis] = slice(None, -w)\n    out[tuple(sl)] = c[tuple(sl)] - c[tuple(sl2)]\n    return out\n\n\ndef rca_panel(x: np.ndarray, GF: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"x [C, NY, 26] counts; GF [NY, 26] venue-field base totals. Portfolio masks [C, NY, 26] evaluated AT year y\n    (the risk-set code reads them at y = t-1). RCA > 1 (strict).\"\"\"\n    x = x.astype(np.float64)\n    GF = GF.astype(np.float64)\n    r1 = _rca(x, GF[None])\n    xw, Gw = rolling(x, 3, 1), rolling(GF, 3, 0)\n    rw = _rca(xw, Gw[None])\n    rc = _rca(np.cumsum(x, 1), np.cumsum(GF, 0)[None])\n    Uw = rw > 1\n    Uw_prev = np.zeros_like(Uw)\n    Uw_prev[:, 3:] = Uw[:, :-3]                 # window y-5..y-3\n    return {\"U_1y\": r1 > 1, \"U_w3\": Uw, \"U_cum\": rc > 1, \"U_pers\": Uw & Uw_prev, \"rca_1y\": r1.astype(np.float32),\n            \"ties_1y\": int(np.isclose(r1, 1.0, rtol=0, atol=1e-12).sum())}\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- strata\nSTRATUM_MASKS = [\"E\", \"ENTOFF\", \"RET\", \"LOST\", \"POOL\", \"HOME\", \"U_1y\", \"U_w3\", \"U_cum\", \"U_pers\",\n                 \"RET_a2\", \"RET_a3\", \"RET_a4p\", \"LOST_s\", \"LOST_l\"]\n\n\ndef build_strata(frame: pd.DataFrame, G: np.ndarray, GF: np.ndarray, *, horizon: int = 10, min_n: float = 2,\n                 entry_def: str = \"count\") -> dict:\n    \"\"\"frame rows aligned with G (row i <-> G[i]); needs columns cidx, t0, home_list (list[int]).\n    Returns per-stratum arrays (masks [S, 26] at t-1, counts, candidates, events) + stratum meta.\"\"\"\n    C = len(frame)\n    home = np.zeros((C, NF), bool)\n    for i, hl in enumerate(frame.home_list):\n        for h in hl:\n            home[i, h - 11] = True\n    S = panel_states(G, home, min_n)\n    R = rca_panel(S[\"x\"], GF)\n    ent = rca_entered_panel(G, GF, min_n) if entry_def == \"rca\" else S[\"entered\"]\n    t0 = frame.t0.to_numpy().astype(int)\n    ci_l, t_l = [], []\n    for i in range(C):\n        for t in range(t0[i] + 1, min(t0[i] + horizon, Y1) + 1):\n            ci_l.append(i); <header class="top">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Concepts spread where they stick: network signals of interdisciplinary diffusion in science</h1>
    <p class="byline">A study of <span data-bind="none">12,499</span> concepts identified in the full OpenAlex snapshot (476 million works).</p>

    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>

  </ul>

<main id="main">
<!-- ============ FINDING ============ -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="finding">
    <div class="prose">
      <p class="q">When a new concept enters one more scientific field, which field does it pick?</p>
      <p class="lede">A field related to the fields that have adopted the concept <em>and kept publishing on it</em>. This holds beyond relatedness to the concept's home field, field size and the usual density measures.</p>
      <p>The paper tests this with a <button class="term" data-term="clogit">conditional logit</button> over each concept's <button class="term" data-term="riskset">risk set</button> of not-yet-entered fields. The coefficient on <button class="term" data-term="d0">retained-frontier relatedness <i>d</i><sub>0</sub></button>, scored once on held-out field groups, is:</p>
      <p class="big num" id="headline-num">&nbsp;<small id="headline-sub"></small></p>
      <p>It is positive in all four held-out domain groups and in the 2010–2014 onset cohort. The gain in discrimination is small, though, and a volume-matched contrast is null, so the paper's own preregistered verdict is <strong>partial</strong>: persistence is confounded with volume.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="panel" id="headline-view">
      <div class="tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Headline view">
        <button role="tab" id="tab-forest" aria-controls="pane-forest" aria-selected="true">By domain group</button>
        <button role="tab" id="tab-ladder" aria-controls="pane-ladder" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1">Against the baseline ladder</button>
      </div>
      <div role="tabpanel" id="pane-forest" aria-labelledby="tab-forest">
        <p class="q">Does the retained-frontier effect hold in every held-out group?</p>
        <div class="controls">
          <span class="lab" id="lab-ci">Interval</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-ci" id="ci-type">
            <button role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="wald">Wald, concept-clustered SE</button>
            <button role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="boot" tabindex="-1">Concept bootstrap</button>
          </div>
          <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="show-vm"> Show the volume-matched contrast</label>

  <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
  <ul class="prose fails">
    <li><strong>Retention is not separated from volume.</strong> The preregistered <button class="term" data-term="vm">volume-matched contrast</button> is null, <span class="num">−0.028 [−0.105, +0.046]</span>, so the frontier verdict is partial.</li>
    <li><strong>The effect depends on how relatedness is measured.</strong> Under <button class="term" data-term="mincp">minimum conditional-probability proximity</button> the coefficient reverses to <span class="num">−0.021</span> (<i>p</i> = 0.012) and adds no AUC.</li>
    <li><strong>Discrimination barely moves.</strong> <button class="term" data-term="auc">Within-stratum AUC</button> rises from 0.847 to 0.852; field size alone reaches 0.76 and density 0.59, with only 26 fields.</li>
    <li><strong>Hub fields do not keep concepts.</strong> The adopting field's <button class="term" data-term="gateway">gateway centrality</button> adds Δ-AUC −0.00001 [−0.0006, +0.0003] for retention on held-out episodes. Verdict: disconfirmed.</li>
    <li><strong>Math &amp; Decision Sciences is underpowered</strong> in both the indicator screen (165 concepts) and the entry model (<i>d</i><sub>0</sub> = 0.065, interval includes zero).</li>
    <li><strong>Little forecasting value.</strong> OPEN adds +0.002 Spearman over the popularity baseline on the fresh cohort; the indicators characterise rather than forecast.</li>
    <li><strong>Held-out outcomes had been read before.</strong> Two earlier experiments unsealed them, so the screen's held-out results are robustness checks; only the 2015–2017 cohort was never used in any prior step.</li>
    <li><strong>Observational.</strong> Early structure correlates with later breadth, but the within-concept panel points to a trait across concepts, not a mechanism inside one concept's trajectory.</li>
  </ul>

    <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@main/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
    <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them">Code repository</a>
  </div>
  <h3>Where each view's data comes from</h3>
  <ul class="prov" id="prov"></ul>
  <h3>Glossary</h3>
  <dl class="gloss" id="gloss">
    <dt id="gt-clogit">Conditional logit</dt><dd id="def-clogit">A discrete choice model that estimates the probability of entry into each candidate field within a stratified choice set. Here it is fitted by Breslow partial likelihood, stratified by each combination of concept and year.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-riskset">Risk set</dt><dd id="def-riskset">At each year after onset, every off-home field that the concept has not yet entered is at risk. The risk set is indexed by concept, target field and year.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-d0">Retained-frontier relatedness <i>d</i><sub>0</sub></dt><dd id="def-d0">The mean backbone relatedness between the target field and the set of off-home fields currently retaining the concept. Its coefficient is expressed in log-odds per standard deviation.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-retain">Retaining field</dt><dd id="def-retain">An off-home field that has adopted a concept and kept publishing on it.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-home">Home field</dt><dd id="def-home">A field holding at least 40% of a concept's first 30 grounded papers.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-t0">Onset year <i>t</i><sub>0</sub></dt><dd id="def-t0">The first year a concept reaches 20 grounded publications.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-backbone">Field backbone</dt><dd id="def-backbone">A weighted graph over 26 fields, with edge weights given by positive pointwise mutual information (PMI) of topics appearing jointly in the same work within a preonset window (1998–2002).</dd>
    <dt id="gt-o2r">Rarefied cross-field breadth O<sub>2r</sub></dt><dd id="def-o2r">The expected number of distinct venue fields among a fixed-size random draw of 50 papers from a concept's publications in years <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+6 to <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+8, computed by exact hypergeometric rarefaction. Rarefaction separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-b5">Popularity baseline (B5)</dt><dd id="def-b5">Five features: log publication volume at <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+2, publication growth rate, log off-home volume, off-home share, and number of home fields.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-psp">Partial Spearman correlation</dt><dd id="def-psp">The rank correlation between an indicator and the outcome after controlling for the popularity baseline (and, at higher rungs, further controls).</dd>
    <dt id="gt-dl">DerSimonian–Laird pool</dt><dd id="def-dl">A random-effects average of the per-group estimates; I<sup>2</sup> reports how much of their spread reflects genuine heterogeneity across groups.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-holm">Holm–Bonferroni correction</dt><dd id="def-holm">A stepdown procedure controlling the familywise error rate across the indicators tested.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-auc">Within-stratum AUC</dt><dd id="def-auc">AUC computed within each concept-year stratum: how well a model ranks the entered field above the fields not entered in the same choice set.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-mincp">Minimum conditional-probability proximity</dt><dd id="def-mincp">An alternative relatedness between fields, following Hidalgo et al. (2007), used as a sensitivity rebuild in place of backbone PMI.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-vm">Volume-matched contrast</dt><dd id="def-vm">The preregistered comparison of entry rates of retained versus fields that were entered but not retained, in the same volume cell.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-gateway">Gateway centrality</dt><dd id="def-gateway">A field's eigenvector centrality on the backbone.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-open">Openness index OPEN<sub>home</sub></dt><dd id="def-open">The mean of six <i>z</i>-scored ego-network components, with constants frozen on the full frame of all 12,499 concepts, measured within the home field.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-nov">Neighbourhood novelty</dt><dd id="def-nov">The share of new partners among a concept's co-occurrence neighbours.</dd>
    <dt id="gt-decomp">Early contact, frontier advance, retention</dt><dd id="def-decomp">Early contact E<sub>2</sub> counts fields entered by <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+2; frontier advance M is the ratio of fields entered by <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+8 to those entered by <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+2; retention ρ is the share of entered fields retained at <i>t</i><sub>0</sub>+8. Their logs add up to the log of retained off-home breadth.</dd>
  </dl>
</div>
</footer>

solid transparent;border-radius:6px 6px 0 0}\n.tabs .hit{stroke:var(--focus);stroke-width:2;fill:rgba(242,169,0,.08)}\n.legend{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px 16px;font-size:14px;color:var(--ink2);margin:6px 0 0}\n.legend span{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}\n.sw{display:inline-block;width:14px;height:14px;border-radius:3px}\n#tip{position:absolute;z-index:50;max-width:300px;background:#1b1f24;color:#fff;font-size:14px;line-height:1.45;padding:8px b{color:#fff}\n.term{font:inherit;color:inherit;background:none;border:0;padding:0 1px;border-bottom:1.5px dotted var(--accent);cursor:help;min-height:0;line-height:inherit}\n.term:hover{color:var(--accent)}\n#termtip{position:absolute;z-index:60;max-width:320px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid #b9bec5;box-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.12);font-size:15px;line-height:1.5;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:8px;display:none}\n#termtip.on{display:block}\n#termtip strong{display:block;margin-bottom:2px}\n/* stepper */\n.stepper .markers{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;list-style:none;padding:0;margin:8px 0}\n.stepper .markers button[aria-current=\"step\"]{background:var(--accent);color:#fff;border-color:var(--accent)}\n.stagegrid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:12px}\n@media(min-width:900px){.stagegrid{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,5fr) button:disabled{border-color:var(--rule);color:#a3a9b0;cursor:not-allowed}\n.chips{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px}\n.chip{font-size:13px;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:14px;border:1px solid solid var(--warn);outline-offset:1px;color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}\ntable{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:14px;width:100%}\nth,td{padding:5px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid td{background:var(--warn-soft);font-weight:600}\n.scrollx{overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%}\n.scrolly{max-height:340px;overflow:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px}\n/* browser */\n.browser{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:16px}\n@media(min-width:900px){.browser{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,4fr) minmax(0,8fr)}}\n.list{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;max-height:560px;overflow:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}\n.list button{display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;font:inherit;font-size:15px;padding:8px 12px;min-height:44px;border:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--grid);background:#fff;color:var(--ink);cursor:pointer}\n.list button[aria-pressed=\"true\"]{background:var(--accent-soft);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent)}\n.list .meta{display:block;font-size:13px;color:var(--muted)}\n.badge{display:inline-block;font-size:12px;padding:1px 7px;border-radius:10px;margin-left:6px;vertical-align:1px}\n.badge.up{background:#e1f1e8;color:#12603f}.badge.down{background:var(--warn-soft);color:#8a4500}.badge.same{background:#eef0f2;color:#4d555e}\n.count{font-size:15px;color:var(--ink2);margin:6px 0}\n.cols2{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:12px}\n@media(min-width:700px){.cols2{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}}\n.stat{background:#f5f6f7;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px}\n.stat .v{font-size:24px;font-weight:700;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}\n.stat .l{font-size:14px;color:var(--muted)}\n.fails li{margin-bottom:10px}\nfooter{border-top:1px solid var(--rule);background:var(--panel);margin-top:48px;padding:32px 0 48px;font-size:16px}\ndl.gloss dt{font-weight:700;margin-top:10px}\ndl.gloss dd{margin:2px 0 0 0;color:var(--ink2);max-width:75ch}\n.prov li{margin-bottom:6px}\ncode{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.88em;background:#f1f2f4;padding:1px 0);white-space:nowrap}\n.note{font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)}\n@media(max-width:600px){body{font-size:17px}.wrap{padding:0 16px}.panel{padding:12px}section.block{padding-top:36px}}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n<header class=\"top\">\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <p class=\"kicker\">Interactive companion to the paper</p>\n    <h1>Concepts spread where they stick: network signals of interdisciplinary diffusion in science</h1>\n    <p class=\"byline\">A study of <span data-bind=\"none\">12,499</span> concepts identified in the full OpenAlex snapshot (476 million works).</p>\n    <div class=\"links\">\n      <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them\">Code repository</a>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</header>\n<nav class=\"sec\" aria-label=\"Sections\">\n  <ul>\n    <li><a href=\"#finding\">The finding</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#how\">How it works</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#explore\">Explore</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#try\">Try it</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#fails\">Where it fails</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#about\">Data &amp; terms</a></li>\n  </ul>\n</nav>\n<main id=\"main\">\n<!-- ============ FINDING ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"finding\" aria-labelledby=\"h-finding\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-finding\">The finding</h2>\n  <div class=\"finding\">\n    <div class=\"prose\">\n      <p class=\"q\">When a new concept enters one more scientific field, which field does it pick?</p>\n      <p class=\"lede\">A field related to the fields that have adopted the concept <em>and kept publishing on it</em>. This holds beyond relatedness to the concept's home field, field size and the usual density measures.</p>\n      <p>The paper tests this with a <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"clogit\">conditional logit</button> over each concept's <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"riskset\">risk set</button> of not-yet-entered fields. The coefficient on <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"d0\">retained-frontier relatedness <i>d</i><sub>0</sub></button>, scored once on held-out field groups, is:</p>\n      <p class=\"big num\" id=\"headline-num\">&nbsp;<small id=\"headline-sub\"></small></p>\n      <p>It is positive in all four held-out domain groups and in the 2010–2014 onset cohort. The gain in discrimination is small, though, and a volume-matched contrast is null, so the paper's own preregistered verdict is <strong>partial</strong>: persistence is confounded with volume.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"panel\" id=\"headline-view\">\n      <div class=\"tabs\" role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Headline view\">\n        <button role=\"tab\" id=\"tab-forest\" aria-controls=\"pane-forest\" aria-selected=\"true\">By domain group</button>\n        <button role=\"tab\" id=\"tab-ladder\" aria-controls=\"pane-ladder\" aria-selected=\"false\" tabindex=\"-1\">Against the baseline ladder</button>\n      </div>\n      <div role=\"tabpanel\" id=\"pane-forest\" aria-labelledby=\"tab-forest\">\n        <p class=\"q\">Does the retained-frontier effect hold in every held-out group?</p>\n        <div class=\"controls\">\n          <span class=\"lab\" id=\"lab-ci\">Interval</span>\n          <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-ci\" id=\"ci-type\">\n            <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"wald\">Wald, concept-clustered SE</button>\n            <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"boot\" tabindex=\"-1\">Concept bootstrap</button>\n          </div>\n          <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"show-vm\"> Show the volume-matched contrast</label>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"forest-chart\"></div>\n        <div class=\"legend\" id=\"forest-legend\"></div>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"forest-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n      </div>\n      <div role=\"tabpanel\" id=\"pane-ladder\" aria-labelledby=\"tab-ladder\" hidden>\n        <p class=\"q\">How much does the retained-frontier term add over the baseline models?</p>\n        <div class=\"controls\">\n          <span class=\"lab\" id=\"lab-prox\">Relatedness used</span>\n          <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-prox\" id=\"prox-type\">\n            <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"primary\">Backbone PMI (primary)</button>\n            <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"mincp\" tabindex=\"-1\">Min. conditional probability</button>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"ladder-auc\"></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"ladder-lr\"></div>\n        <div class=\"legend\" id=\"ladder-legend\"></div>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"ladder-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ HOW ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"how\" aria-labelledby=\"h-how\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-how\">How it works: one concept, one year, one choice</h2>\n  <p class=\"prose\">The stepper follows one real record from the held-out frame, <strong id=\"ex-name\"></strong>, through the stages that produce the two probabilities the run recorded for every candidate field. Use the buttons, the stage markers, or the left and right arrow keys.</p>\n  <div class=\"panel stepper\" id=\"stepper\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-roledescription=\"stepper\">\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"pipe\"></div>\n    <ol class=\"markers\" id=\"markers\" aria-label=\"Stages\"></ol>\n    <p class=\"sr\" aria-live=\"polite\" id=\"step-live\"></p>\n    <div class=\"stagegrid\">\n      <div>\n        <h3 id=\"stage-title\" style=\"margin-top:4px\"></h3>\n        <dl class=\"io\" id=\"stage-io\"></dl>\n      </div>\n      <div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"stage-vis\"></div>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"navbtns\">\n      <button id=\"prev\" type=\"button\">&larr; Previous</button>\n      <button id=\"next\" type=\"button\">Next &rarr;</button>\n      <span class=\"note\" id=\"step-count\"></span>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ EXPLORE ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"explore\" aria-labelledby=\"h-explore\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-explore\">Explore the evidence</h2>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-browser\">Every choice, side by side</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">For a given concept-year, does adding retained-frontier relatedness move the field that was actually entered up the ranking?</p>\n  <p class=\"prose note\" id=\"browser-rule\"></p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label for=\"f-unit\">Group</label>\n      <select id=\"f-unit\"></select>\n      <label for=\"f-search\">Concept</label>\n      <input type=\"search\" id=\"f-search\" placeholder=\"Search by name\" autocomplete=\"off\">\n      <label for=\"f-sort\">Sort</label>\n      <select id=\"f-sort\">\n        <option value=\"gain\">Largest rank gain first</option>\n        <option value=\"loss\">Largest rank loss first</option>\n        <option value=\"name\">Concept name</option>\n        <option value=\"year\">Year</option>\n      </select>\n      <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"f-fail\"> Only where the model ranks the entered field lower</label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"count\" id=\"b-count\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"browser\">\n      <ul class=\"list\" id=\"b-list\" aria-label=\"Concept-year strata\"></ul>\n      <div>\n        <div id=\"b-head\"></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"b-chart\"></div>\n        <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>Baseline R2 probability</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>With retained frontier (R3)</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#fff;border:2px solid var(--warn)\"></i>Field actually entered</span></div>\n        <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"b-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-ind\">Which early network signals carry information beyond popularity?</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">Does each frozen indicator hold in every held-out body, or only on average?</p>\n  <p class=\"prose\">Each indicator was chosen on the development set and then scored by <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"psp\">partial Spearman correlation</button> with <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"o2r\">rarefied cross-field breadth</button> given the <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"b5\">popularity baseline</button>, in four held-out domain groups and two 2010–2014 cohort bodies.</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label for=\"i-out\">Outcome</label>\n      <select id=\"i-out\"><option value=\"O2r_m50\">Rarefied breadth O2r (m = 50)</option><option value=\"O2r_resid\">Size-residualised breadth</option></select>\n      <label for=\"i-ind\">Indicator</label>\n      <select id=\"i-ind\"></select>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"ind-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Held-out body (95% CI)</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--ink)\"></i>DL pool of the four groups</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#fff;border:1.5px dashed #7a828b\"></i>Zero: no signal beyond B5</span></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"ind-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <h4>Combining them: a learned model against the baseline</h4>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"learn-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>Popularity baseline B5</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>ElasticNet on the frozen indicators</span></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"learn-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-dec\">Why do some concepts end up broad? Contact, advance, or retention</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">Is the breadth gap between integrating and localised concepts set early, or built later?</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label for=\"d-body\">Body</label>\n      <select id=\"d-body\"></select>\n      <span class=\"lab\" id=\"lab-dv\">Variant</span>\n      <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-dv\" id=\"d-var\">\n        <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"iv_vol_noMed_PR1\">Volume-stratified, no Medicine</button>\n        <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"i_pooled\" tabindex=\"-1\">Unstratified</button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"dec-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--green)\"></i>Early contact E<sub>2</sub></span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#b8bec5\"></i>Frontier advance M</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Retention ρ</span></div>\n    <div class=\"scrollx\"><table id=\"dec-table\" aria-label=\"Top versus bottom tercile averages\"></table></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"dec-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ TRY ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"try\" aria-labelledby=\"h-try\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-try\">Try it</h2>\n  <h3 style=\"margin-top:8px\">How often is the entered field near the top of the list?</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">If you shortlisted the <i>k</i> most likely fields for each concept-year, how often would the field it actually entered be on the list?</p>\n  <p class=\"prose note\">Computed live from the probabilities the run recorded for all <span id=\"k-nstrata\"></span> held-out concept-years (<span id=\"k-nevents\"></span> entries), scored with coefficients frozen on the development set. The paper does not report this hit rate; it is a reading of the same predictions.</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label for=\"k-range\">Shortlist size <i>k</i></label>\n      <input type=\"range\" id=\"k-range\" min=\"1\" max=\"10\" step=\"1\" value=\"3\" aria-describedby=\"k-out\">\n      <output id=\"k-out\" class=\"num\" for=\"k-range\"></output>\n      <label for=\"k-unit\">Group</label>\n      <select id=\"k-unit\"></select>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"k-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--base)\"></i>Baseline R2</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>With retained frontier R3</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#fff;border:1.5px dashed #7a828b\"></i>Random shortlist</span></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"k-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3>Run the frozen model yourself</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">What if one of the fields that retain the concept had dropped it?</p>\n  <p class=\"prose\">The model is small enough to run here exactly: standardise the seven recorded covariates with the development-set means and SDs, weight them by the frozen coefficients, and take a softmax within the concept-year. Untick a retaining field and the page recomputes <i>d</i><sub>0</sub> for every candidate as the mean backbone relatedness to the fields still ticked. The other covariates stay at their recorded values, so this is the model's counterfactual, not an observed one.</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <p id=\"t-case\" class=\"count\"></p>\n    <fieldset style=\"border:0;padding:0;margin:0\"><legend class=\"lab\" style=\"font-size:15px;color:var(--ink2)\">Fields retaining the concept in the previous year</legend><div class=\"controls\" id=\"t-ret\"></div></fieldset>\n    <div class=\"cols2\" id=\"t-stats\"></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"t-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#b8bec5\"></i>Recorded R3 probability</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--accent)\"></i>Recomputed with your retained set</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#fff;border:2px solid var(--warn)\"></i>Field actually entered</span></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"t-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"note\">Pick another concept-year in the browser above and it loads here.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ FAILS ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"fails\" aria-labelledby=\"h-fails\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-fails\">Where it fails</h2>\n  <p class=\"q\">In how many recorded choices does the retained-frontier model do worse than the baseline?</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label for=\"x-unit\">Group</label>\n      <select id=\"x-unit\"></select>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"cols2\" id=\"x-stats\"></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"x-chart\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--green)\"></i>Entered field ranked higher by R3</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#b8bec5\"></i>Same rank</span><span><i class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--warn)\"></i>Ranked lower by R3</span></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway warn\" id=\"x-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"navbtns\"><button type=\"button\" id=\"x-go\">Show the failures in the browser</button></div>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3>The openness signal is weaker than the in-sample estimate</h3>\n  <p class=\"q\">Does the home-field openness index hold outside the body it was chosen on?</p>\n  <div class=\"panel\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <span class=\"lab\" id=\"lab-ef\">Index</span>\n      <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-ef\" id=\"e-feat\">\n        <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"OPEN_home\">OPEN<sub>home</sub></button>\n        <button role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"NOVCHURN_home\" tabindex=\"-1\">Novelty and churn</button>\n      </div>\n      <label for=\"e-rung\">Controls</label>\n      <select id=\"e-rung\"><option value=\"R0\">R0: popularity baseline + onset year</option><option value=\"R2\" selected>R2: + contact reach (paper's       el(main ? "circle" : "rect", main ? {cx: sx(i), cy: sy(v), r: 6, fill: col} : {x: sx(i) - 4.5, y: sy(v) - 4.5, width: 9, height: 9, fill: col}, g);
      const specN = D === L.primary ? "Backbone PMI" : "Min. conditional probability";
      markify(g, `${names[i]}, ${specN}: AUC ${v.toFixed(3)}`, `<b>${names[i]}</b><br>${specN}<br>Within-stratum AUC ${v.toFixed(3)}`);
    });
  });
  // LR panel
  const C2 = $("#ladder-lr"), H2 = 200;
  const lrs = A.LR.slice(1), mx = Math.max(...lrs, 3.84) * 1.1;
  const xT = niceTicks(0, mx, narrow ? 3 : 5), m2 = {l: 22 + Math.max(...xT.map(t => textW(String(t), 12))) + 14, r: 16, t: 12, b: narrow ? 34 : 38};
  const s2 = newSvg(C2, W, H2, "Likelihood-ratio statistic for each added term");
  const bx = i => m2.l + (i + 0.5) * (W - m2.l - m2.r) / 3, by = v => m2.t + (1 - v / mx) * (H2 - m2.t - m2.b);
  xT.forEach(t => { el("line", {x1: m2.l, x2: W - m2.r, y1: by(t), y2: by(t), class: "gl"}, s2); tx(s2, m2.l - 6, by(t) + 4, String(t), {class: "tick", "text-anchor": "end"}); });
  tx(s2, 0, 0, "LR χ² (df = 1)", {class: "axt", "text-anchor": "middle", transform: `translate(${m2.l - Math.max(...xT.map(t => textW(String(t), 12))) - 16},${(m2.t + H2 - m2.b) / 2}) rotate(-90)`});
  el("line", {x1: m2.l, x2: W - m2.r, y1: by(3.84), y2: by(3.84), stroke: "var(--ink)", "stroke-dasharray": "2 3"}, s2);
  const lblTxt = narrow ? ["+RCA", "+volume", "+retained"] : ["R1 vs R0: +RCA density", "R2 vs R1: +volume density", "R3 vs R2: +retained frontier"];

    el("rect", {x: bx(i) - bw / 2, y: by(v), width: bw, height: by(0) - by(v), fill: col}, g);
    tx(g, bx(i), by(v) - 5, v.toFixed(1), {"text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 12, fill: "var(--ink)"});
    const p = A.p[i + 1];
    markify(g, `${lblTxt[i]}: LR ${v.toFixed(1)}`, `<b>${lblTxt[i]}</b><br>LR = ${v.toFixed(1)}, p = ${p < 1e-4 ? p.toExponential(1) : p.toFixed(3)}<br>dotted line: p = 0.05 (χ² = 3.84)`);
    tx(s2, bx(i), H2 - m2.b + 18, lblTxt[i], {class: "tick", "text-anchor": "middle"});

/* tabs */
(function tabs() {
  const tabs = [$("#tab-forest"), $("#tab-ladder")];
  const sel = (t, focus) => { tabs.forEach(x => { const on = x === t; x.setAttribute("aria-selected", on); x.tabIndex = on ? 0 : -1; document.getElementById(x.getAttribute("aria-controls")).hidden = !on; }); if (focus) t.focus(); redrawAll(); };
  tabs.forEach((t, i) => { t.addEventListener("click", () => sel(t)); t.addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.key === "ArrowRight" || e.key === "ArrowLeft") { e.preventDefault(); sel(tabs[(i + 1) % 2], true); } }); });
